newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SCORE 309 RUNS AGAINST PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA SCORE 309 RUNS AGAINST PAKISTAN.

text.p: A breezy start aided by a middle order onslaught helped world champions Sri Lanka amass 309 in 49.4 overs against Pakistan in the second match of the Independence Cup final on Tuesday.

Sri Lanka, who won the first final by 115 runs in Mohali on Saturday, were led by skipper Arjuna Ranatunga, who won the toss, elected to bat, played some judicious shots and top-scored with 59 runs off 78 balls with three fours and one six.
He shared steady partnerships of 67 runs with Aravinda De Silva for the fourth wicket and 73 runs with Hashan Tillekeratne for the fifth.
Ranatunga was run out by offspinner Saqlain Mushtaq while trying to steal a single off his bowling.
Sri Lanka, helped by some big hits by opener Sanath Jayasuriya, raced to their 50 in just 32 minutes off 44 balls.
Left-handed Jayasuriya, who was dropped by Saeed Anwar at 21 at cover point off the bowling of Aqib Javed, went on to score 55 runs off 40 balls, aided by seven fours and two sixes.

Jayasuriya and Marvan Atapattu scored 69 runs for the opening partnership. Atapattu was caught at short mid-wicket while trying to flick off-break bowler Hassan Raza. He was caught at gully by substitute fielder Azhar Mahmood while trying to steer a ball off Arshad Khan.
Romesh Kaluwitharana, who came in at the fall of Atapattu, did not survive long, trapped leg before by leg spinner Shahid Afridi.
Arvinda De Silva, who came in after the fall of Jayasuriya's wicket, pushed up the score along with his captain.
De Silva, who made 57 runs off 49 balls, had his middle stump uprooted by a ball from Mushtaq which went through his bat and pad. He hit eight fours in his exuberant knock.
Left-handed Hassan Tillekeratne scored 38 runs off 48 balls with the help of two fours and one six.
Sri Lanka lost their last three wickets in 5 balls.
Saqlain was the most successful bowler for Pakistan claiming four wickets for 53 runs off his 9.4 overs.
